source.title: Major milestone reached in ending building safety crisis
source.venue_label: Press release (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)

drafts.quote: The Bill brings forward a new legal duty on those responsible for the safety of their buildings, such as freeholders, to identify, assess, and fix issues without delay – anyone who obstructs this work could face criminal penalties.

speaker.name: HM Government
speaker.role: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

suggested.who: Those responsible for building safety, such as freeholders

drafts.why: The Bill will create a legal duty on those responsible for building safety, such as freeholders, to identify, assess and fix cladding issues, with criminal penalties for anyone who obstructs the work.

drafts.quote: In addition, there will be a stronger enforcement framework to sanction responsible entity that fail to comply with a Remediation Order, enabling the First-tier Tribunal to hand down financial penalties of up to £500,000.

speaker.name: HM Government
speaker.role: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

suggested.who: Responsible entities failing to comply with Remediation Orders

drafts.why: Through the Remediation of Unsafe Cladding Bill, the First-tier Tribunal will gain the power to fine those who fail to comply with a Remediation Order up to £500,000.

drafts.quote: The expectation remains that by the end of 2029, every building over 11 metres with unsafe cladding should either have been remediated or have a clear date for completion – the key change being that tougher powers will become available before this.

speaker.name: HM Government
speaker.role: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

suggested.who: Residents of buildings over 11 metres with unsafe cladding

drafts.why: Restates the earlier Remediation Acceleration Plan target that, by the end of 2029, every building over 11 metres with unsafe cladding will be remediated or have a clear completion date. Editors should quote the original commitment.

drafts.quote: As a safety net, third parties, such as Homes England or local authorities, will be able to step in and carry out remediation if those responsible continuously fail to act – reassuring residents that works will go ahead.

speaker.name: HM Government
speaker.role: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

suggested.who: Residents of buildings where responsible parties fail to act; Homes England; local authorities

drafts.why: The Bill will give third parties such as Homes England or local authorities the power to carry out remediation where those responsible repeatedly fail to act.

drafts.quote: A new register of all medium rise residential buildings in England will help ensure no building falls through the net. Failure to register could result in civil penalties of up to £7,000 with higher financial penalties of up to £40,000 or prosecution available.

speaker.name: HM Government
speaker.role: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

suggested.who: Owners of medium rise residential buildings in England
suggested.how_much: civil penalties of up to £7,000; higher penalties of up to £40,000

drafts.why: The Bill will create a register of all medium-rise residential buildings in England, with civil penalties of up to £7,000 and higher penalties of up to £40,000 or prosecution for failing to register.

drafts.quote: Fire risk appraisals of external walls (FRAEWs) – which help determine whether remediation is needed – will be required to follow a consistent approach to assessment, where buildings are judged on the same basis, and risks identified through independently audited, evidence-based assessments.

speaker.name: HM Government
speaker.role: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

drafts.why: The Bill will require fire risk appraisals of external walls (FRAEWs) to follow a consistent, independently audited assessment approach.

drafts.quote: And where an assessment recommends remedial work, responsible entities will be required to share a plan with residents, setting out the steps and proposed timescales for remediating each building they are responsible for.

speaker.name: HM Government
speaker.role: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

suggested.who: Residents of buildings where remediation is recommended; responsible entities

drafts.why: The Bill will require responsible entities to share a remediation plan, with steps and timescales, with residents wherever an assessment recommends remedial work.
